summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with sepsis secondary to a chronic right hip wound and suspected osteomyelitis, with additional concerns for urinary tract infection and suprapubic pain. He was transferred from an outside hospital where he had been treated with Unasyn, which was discontinued due to prior resistance and allergies. He started IV daptomycin for Enterococcus infection, to which the organism was sensitive, and oral metronidazole for anaerobic coverage after wound cultures grew Enterococcus and Prevotella. He underwent irrigation and debridement of the right hip with flap grafting and primary closure. Postoperatively, he was maintained on strict bedrest in the left lateral decubitus position with head elevation under 30 degrees. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotic administration. His condition stabilized, with controlled pain, stable renal function, and no signs of active UTI. He was discharged to an extended care facility on a 14-day course of daptomycin and metronidazole, with follow-up planned for drain removal and wound monitoring.
